stt.title: Transcription

local.name: Local · Parakeet
local.hint: On your Mac: audio never leaves the machine and it works offline. Needs the models below.

deepgram.name: Cloud · Deepgram
deepgram.hint: Low latency and strong on difficult audio; audio is sent to Deepgram's servers. The API key stays in the macOS Keychain: create one at console.deepgram.com.

llm.title: Language model

ollama.name: Ollama (local)
ollama.hint: Runs on your Mac: nothing leaves the machine and no key is needed. Start Ollama and pull a model (e.g. ollama pull qwen3:8b).

opencode.name: OpenCode Zen
opencode.hint: Pay-per-use cloud (Zen credits). The API key stays in the macOS Keychain: create it in the opencode.ai console under Account → Personal API keys. Only compatible models (chat completions) are listed.

opencode-go.name: OpenCode Go
opencode-go.hint: OpenCode Go subscription, same console API key (Account → Personal API keys). Go is meant for coding agents and traffic is monitored: meeting use may get the account limited. Only compatible models are listed.

openai.name: OpenAI
openai.hint: Pay-per-use cloud. The API key stays in the macOS Keychain: create it on platform.openai.com → API keys. Only chat models are listed (e.g. gpt-5.4-mini for translation).

anthropic.name: Anthropic (Claude)
anthropic.hint: Pay-per-use cloud, Claude's native API. The API key stays in the macOS Keychain: create it on platform.claude.com → API keys. claude-haiku-5-5 is enough for translation.

custom.name: Custom
custom.hint: Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Groq, OpenRouter, LM Studio…). The key is optional and stays in the Keychain.

llm.translationHint: Small and fast: translates the others' sentences.
llm.autoTranslateHint: Translates every sentence from the others. Off: use the “Translate” button next to the sentence.
llm.targetHint: Language you read the others' sentences in.
llm.autoSummaryHint: On stop, generate overview, key points and action items.
llm.translateMineHint: Shows under each of your sentences how to say it in the others' language (the one set or detected from what they say).

localOnly.title: Local only
localOnly.hint: For confidential meetings: transcription on your Mac and a language model only on Ollama or a localhost endpoint. No data leaves the machine during the session.
localOnly.violation: The selected language model runs in the cloud: with "Local only" the session won't start. Switch to Ollama or a localhost endpoint, or clear the translation and suggestion models.

speakers.title: Recognize speakers
speakers.hint: Tells apart who is speaking among the other participants (Speaker 1, 2…). Runs locally and needs the CAM++ model.
speakers.countHint: If you know how many there are, recognition is steadier and fixes sentences already shown.

duringCall.title: During the call
duringCall.widgetHint: The widget stays above Teams, Meet or Zoom with translations, suggestions and nudges, and is hidden from screen sharing. Open it from the button at the top, the menu bar icon or with ⌥⌘S.
duringCall.nudgesHint: Warns you if you talk too much or too fast, if a monologue drags on or if you haven't asked any questions yet. At most one every 2 minutes.
duringCall.liveAssistHint: What to say and what to ask, generated every 20 s from the conversation (live assist). You can turn them on and off during the call too.

search.title: History search
search.hint: Find meetings by meaning too, in any language: “server costs” finds “la bolletta AWS è troppo alta”. The model runs on your Mac; the index sits next to the transcripts and is deleted with the meeting.
search.toggleHint: Indexes meetings in the background, at low priority, when they end.
search.downloadHint: Download EmbeddingGemma 2 (about 206 MB): it stays on your Mac and works offline too.

voices.title: Voice profiles
voices.hint: Recognizes speakers you have named in later meetings. A voiceprint is biometric data: it stays on this Mac only (even with Deepgram), is never sent over the network, and is saved only for named speakers after at least 20 seconds of speech.
voices.toggleHint: Off by default. When the voice is a close match the name is assigned, otherwise it is suggested.
voices.needsDiarization: "Recognize speakers" must also be on (Transcription card).
voices.empty: No saved profiles. Name a speaker during a call to create one.
voices.deleteAllConfirm: The saved voiceprints will be erased from this Mac. This cannot be undone.
voices.offConfirm: Do you also want to delete the saved profiles? If you keep them, they stay on this Mac but are not used.

settings.echoCancellationHint: Without headphones the microphone picks up the others' voices from the speakers: this removes them before transcription, so their sentences don't end up under "Me". Not needed with headphones, but harmless.

email.title: Email

email.passwordHint: Stored in the macOS Keychain. For Gmail, iCloud and Outlook use an app password.

guide.title: How to set up Google Cloud (one time only)
guide.intro: Sottovoce connects with an OAuth client you create yourself: data goes from your calendar straight to the app, with no server in between. It takes about 10 minutes.

project.title: Create a project
project.body: Sign in to Google Cloud Console with your Google account and create a project, for example "Sottovoce". You don't need to enable billing.

api.title: Enable the Google Calendar API
api.body: With the project selected open APIs & Services → Library, search for "Google Calendar API" and click Enable.

branding.title: Set up the consent screen
branding.body: Open Google Auth Platform → Branding (click Get started the first time): app name "Sottovoce", your email as support email and developer contact.

audience.title: Choose the audience
audience.body:
In Audience choose "Internal" if you have Google Workspace and will use Sottovoce only within your organization: no verification and no warning.
Otherwise choose "External", then click Publish app to move to "In production": in Testing mode access expires every 7 days.

scopes.title: Add the calendar permission
scopes.body: In Data access click Add or remove scopes, search and check ".../auth/calendar.events.readonly" (read-only events), then Update and Save.

client.title: Create the OAuth client
client.body: In Clients click Create client, application type "Desktop app", name "Sottovoce", then Create. Copy the client ID and client secret from the dialog that appears (you can reopen it from the client).

paste.title: Connect Sottovoce
paste.body: Paste the client ID and client secret in the fields above and click "Connect Google Calendar": the browser opens, pick the account and allow calendar access (keep the calendar box checked).

warning.title: If you see "Google hasn't verified this app"
warning.body: With an "External" audience and no verification this is expected: it's the client you just created. Click Advanced → Go to Sottovoce. Without verification the client works for up to 100 users.

guide.privacy: Sottovoce only reads events from your primary calendar (read-only), from yesterday to the next 30 days, and imports only those with a Meet, Teams or Zoom link that you haven't declined. The client secret and access stay in the Keychain.

microsoft.title: Outlook / Microsoft 365
microsoft.hint: Meetings in your Outlook calendar with a Teams, Zoom or Meet link show up in the Schedule by themselves, ready to start.
microsoft.tenantHint: Leave empty if the app accepts accounts in any organization and personal accounts; otherwise the directory ID or domain (e.g. contoso.onmicrosoft.com).
microsoft.needClient: Enter the client ID (see the guide below).
microsoft.needsReconnect: Access to Outlook expired or was revoked: reconnect the calendar.
microsoft.disconnectConfirm: Sottovoce forgets the access and imported meetings leave the Schedule, except the ones you edited. To remove the permission on Microsoft's side too, open myapps.microsoft.com (or account.microsoft.com → Privacy → Apps and services).

guide.title: How to register the app on Microsoft Entra (one time only)
guide.intro: Sottovoce connects with an app you register yourself (public client, no secret): data goes from your calendar straight to the app, with no server in between. It takes about 10 minutes.

signin.title: Sign in to Microsoft Entra
signin.body: Open the Microsoft Entra admin center with your work or school account. With a personal Microsoft account you need a directory: create a free Azure account, or ask IT to register the app for you.

register.title: Register the app
register.body:
Applications → App registrations → New registration. Name "Sottovoce".
Supported account types: "Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts" (or your organization only).
Redirect URI: platform "Public client/native (mobile & desktop)", value http://localhost. Click Register.

ids.title: Copy the IDs
ids.body: From the app Overview copy "Application (client) ID". If the app is for your organization only, also copy "Directory (tenant) ID".

publicClient.title: Allow public client flows
publicClient.body: Authentication → Advanced settings → "Allow public client flows": Yes → Save. Sottovoce doesn't use a client secret.

permissions.title: Add the calendar permission
permissions.body:
API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph → Delegated permissions → check Calendars.Read and offline_access → Add permissions.
If you are an admin click "Grant admin consent": in many companies users can't connect without it.

paste.title: Connect Sottovoce
paste.body: Paste the client ID (and the directory ID if needed) in the fields above and click "Connect Outlook": pick the account in the browser and accept the permissions.

warning.title: If you see "Need admin approval"
warning.body: Your organization doesn't let users authorize external apps: ask IT to grant admin consent to the registered app (API permissions) or to register it for you.

guide.privacy: Sottovoce only reads events from your default calendar (read-only), from yesterday to the next 30 days, and imports only those with a Teams, Zoom or Meet link that you haven't declined. The access stays in the Keychain.

permissions.hint: On first launch macOS asks for microphone and system audio recording permission.

welcome.title: Welcome to Sottovoce
welcome.lead: Your assistant for Teams, Meet and Zoom calls: it listens with you and whispers what you need.
welcome.time: We'll walk you through the setup: it takes a couple of minutes and you can change everything later.

transcribe.title: Transcribes
transcribe.text: You and the others, on two separate channels.

translate.title: Translates
translate.text: Every sentence in your language, in real time.

suggest.title: Suggests
suggest.text: What to say or ask, while you talk.

summarize.title: Summarizes
summarize.text: Key points and to-dos at the end of the call.

languages.title: Which languages are spoken?
languages.lead: A fixed language makes transcription more accurate. You can also pick it for each call.
languages.mineHint: The one you speak and read translations and summaries in.
languages.theirsHint: If it changes from call to call, leave it on "Automatic".

engine.title: Where to transcribe?
engine.lead: Choose whether audio stays on your Mac or goes to a cloud service.

local.title: On your Mac
local.text: Private and free: audio never leaves the computer and it works offline too. You download the models only once.

cloud.title: In the cloud (Deepgram)
cloud.text: A bit faster and more accurate on difficult audio. Needs a Deepgram account, and audio goes to their servers.
cloud.keyHint: Create the key at console.deepgram.com and paste it here: it stays in the macOS Keychain.

engine.localOnlyHint: Guarantees that no data leaves your Mac during calls, including translations and suggestions.

models.title: Download the models
models.lead: They stay on your Mac and work offline. The download keeps going even if you move on.
models.background: Downloading: you can continue the setup.

sttBackup.title: Offline transcription
sttBackup.text: A backup, in case you want to transcribe without the cloud

search.title: Search your history
search.text: Finds meetings by meaning, not just by words

audio.title: Let's test the audio
audio.lead: Sottovoce listens to your microphone and to your Mac's audio (the others in the call). Let's check both come through.
audio.askText: macOS will ask you to allow access. Sottovoce never stores audio.
audio.deniedText: Enable Sottovoce in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone, then come back. You may need to reopen the app.
audio.micHint: Say something: the bar should move.
audio.systemHint: Play a video or a song: the bar should move.
audio.systemSilent: Not moving? Allow Sottovoce to record system audio in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
audio.systemOff: System audio is turned off: you can enable it in Settings.
audio.headphones: With headphones transcription is cleaner; without them, Sottovoce removes the others' echo from your microphone.

ai.title: Translation and summaries
ai.lead: Translating, suggesting and summarizing need a language model. You can also skip this: transcription works anyway.

ollama.title: Ollama on your Mac
ollama.text: Private and free, needs Ollama installed.

cloud.title: Cloud service
cloud.text: OpenAI, Claude or OpenCode, with your own key.

later.title: Later
later.text: Set it up whenever you like in Settings.

ai.localOnly: With "Local only" on, only a model on your Mac can be used.
ai.ollamaMissing: Ollama isn't responding. Install it from ollama.com, open it and try again.
ai.ollamaNoModels: Ollama is running but has no models. Download one from Terminal, for example: ollama pull qwen3:8b
ai.noModels: No compatible model found with this key.
ai.modelHint: Used for translation, suggestions and summaries.

done.title: All set
done.hint: You can change everything in Settings and run this setup again anytime. To begin a call, press "Start".
